USMLE-style practice · Pediatrics

Barking cough at night

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 2-year-old with two days of rhinorrhea awakens with a harsh barking cough and hoarse voice. Inspiratory stridor occurs when crying, but he is playful when calm and has no drooling. Which diagnosis is most likely?

  1. Viral croup
  2. Epiglottitis
  3. Retropharyngeal abscess
  4. Bronchiolitis
  5. Peritonsillar abscess
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Viral croup

The age, viral prodrome, barking cough and hoarseness are typical of croup.

Understanding the options

Viral croup
The age, viral prodrome, barking cough and hoarseness are typical of croup.
Epiglottitis
Epiglottitis more often causes marked dysphagia, drooling and toxicity without a prominent bark.
Retropharyngeal abscess
A deep-neck abscess usually has fever, painful swallowing and neck restriction.
Bronchiolitis
Bronchiolitis predominantly causes lower-airway crackles and wheeze in infants.
Peritonsillar abscess
Quinsy produces focal peritonsillar findings rather than this classic bark.
